en.headline: Police ticket seven Tseung Kwan O youths over night bicycle offences
en.dek: Tseung Kwan O officers said the summonses follow complaints about late-night 'bullet bike' riding without lights and on pavements.
body: Tseung Kwan O police said on Saturday they had prosecuted seven male youths aged 14 to 17 by summons for bicycle offences, after district councillors raised complaints about late-night 'bullet bike' riding in the new town.

The offences cited include riding at night or in low visibility without a white front lamp and a red rear lamp, and riding on a pavement without an obvious need. Officers posted photographs of several intercepted bicycles on the district formation's social media account and said enforcement against illegal use of electric mobility devices was continuing in parallel.

Under the Road Traffic (Traffic Control) Regulations, a person must not ride a bicycle on a road at night or in poor visibility unless a white light is shown at the front and a red light at the rear. Police said they would keep targeting different traffic offences to protect road users, and asked riders to follow the rules.

Residents and councillors have described groups of modified bicycles circulating housing estates after dark, generating noise and close passes on footpaths. The summonses do not amount to arrests; the youths will answer the tickets in the usual way.

zh.headline: 將軍澳警票控7名少年 涉夜間單車無燈及踩行人路
zh.dek: 警區稱近日有區議員反映「子彈仔」深夜擾民，已向14至17歲少年發出傳票。
body: 將軍澳警區周六在社交平台公布，近日以傳票方式檨控7名14至17歲男性青少年，涉及夜間或能見度低時未亮前白後紅車燈，以及沒有明顯需要在行人路騎單車等違法行為，回應區議員對「子彈仔」深夜擾民的反映。
警方同時展示多部被截獲的單車，並指除持續打擊非法使用電動可移動工具外，亦關注單車違法行為。根據《道路交通（交通管制）規例》，任何人不得在黑夜或能見度低時於道路上騎單車，除非車頭展示白燈、車尾展示紅燈。
警方強調會繼續執法，保障道路使用者安全，並呼籲市民遵守交通規則。有居民及區議員指改裝單車深夜在屋邸出沒，製造噪音並在行人路近距離超車。今次以傳票處理，並非拘捕，涉事少年須按程序應訊。
